title: Nalgene FAQ
supports: all bottles dishwasher safe, top rack away from the heating element
freezing: fill only about 2/3 full
Tritan Renew used for the majority of bottles; #7 plastic
note: Gives no temperature range for the bottle; src_hot_water does.

title: Nalgene: Can You Put Boiling Water in a Nalgene? Here's What You Should Know
supports: What Is the Temperature Limit for a Nalgene Bottle? Sustain® Renew bottles: Safe for hot liquids, including boiling water (up to 212°F / 100°C) in everyday use
a current Nalgene bottle is 'made to handle both freezing and boiling temps without cracking, leaking, or melting'
'You can pour boiling water into your Nalgene, but you should never try to boil water in it. These bottles aren't manufactured for direct heat or open flames.'
'After pouring in boiling water, wait a few seconds before screwing on the lid. Steam builds pressure, and tightening the cap too soon can create a seal that's tough to open (or cause leaks later).'
'Avoid direct flame or stove contact ... Doing so can warp the plastic or damage the bottle.'
'Sudden temperature swings can stress even heat-resistant plastic.'
Dishwasher safe, top rack recommended
note: Blog-style article on nalgene.com (datePublished 2026-07-31, dateModified 2026-08-12), not a datasheet. It names the material both 'Tritan Renew' ('Our Nalgene Tritan Renew Water Bottles') and 'Sustain®' / 'Sustain® Renew' for the same bottles; the product page calls this bottle Tritan Renew, so the 100 °C limit for 'Sustain® Renew bottles' is read as applying to it. No minimum temperature is given beyond 'freezing'. Saved as .research/downloads/hot-water.raw.

title: Thermo Scientific Nalgene Bottles and Carboys technical brochure (D01705)
supports: closure is one-piece linerless; seal ring moulded inside the closure fits tightly against the bevelled inner edge (chamfer) of the bottle neck
threads on bottles and closures are continuous, straight-shouldered semi-buttress threads
Recommended application torques: 63-415 minimum 40 in-lb (46 cm-kg), maximum 56 in-lb (64 cm-kg); threads must be dry
note: Thermo Fisher's Nalgene laboratory line (Nalge Nunc), not the consumer Nalgene Outdoor bottle; applied to this bottle as an assumption. pdftotext -layout of the PDF reads the torque table cleanly (p. 'Application Notes').
